subject: chi-square comparison: Lavaan, Lisrel, and EQS

messages.author: d6b65219d5ee044d
messages.subject: chi-square comparison: Lavaan, Lisrel, and EQS
parts:
Hi folks,

I am running a data simulation and comparing the chi-square results generated when fitting different estimating models us lavaan vs using the mimic = "EQS" function within lavaan. Ideally I could use the mimic = "lisrel" function but this is not yet available and I've read that EQS and lisrel have similar properties. 

I have 50 reps of data generated using a population model where different estimating models are fit to these generated datasets.

I have two broad questions:

1. Is the computation of the chi-square statistic going to vary across the programs? It would seem so as I'm getting different results when using lavaan vs when using the mimic = "EQS" function. Perhaps I need to set seeds in a particular manner.

2. Would EQS and lisrel have a similar method of computing the chi-square?

Thanks in advance. 

Chris

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: chi-square comparison: Lavaan, Lisrel, and EQS
parts: I'm not an expert on this topic but, instead of focusing on the chi-square calculation, focus on the solution--the parameter estimates. Programs differ in terms of things like starting value selection and convergence criteria. Historically, I think, LISREL was "tuned" to work best for a well-fitting model, while some packages were optimized for models with an approximate fit, so if your population includes lack of fit, that might induce differences. Check your parameter estimates at a high level of precision, and you may see differences, which would turn into a different Sigma-hat, which would naturally produce a different chi-square. Alternately, you might generate data so as to eliminate lack of fit and / or sampling variance. If you eliminate both of those, then I think differences between programs will disappear (unless maybe your sample size is very small).

messages.author: bc810b1d0900407f
messages.subject: Re: chi-square comparison: Lavaan, Lisrel, and EQS
parts:
I am not 100% certain of all the effects of `mimic` because it affects several aspects of the analysis, not just chi-square. But for chi-square, the following example shows the differences between mimic = "lavaan" (the default) and mimic = "eqs":

```r
# From the example of cfa()

library(lavaan)
#> This is lavaan 0.6-15
#> lavaan is FREE software! Please report any bugs.
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
              textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
              speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

fit_lavaan <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, mimic = "lavaan")
fit_eqs <- cfa(HS.model, data = HolzingerSwineford1939, mimic = "eqs")

# Likelihood approach (see "likelihood" in the help page of lavOptions())
fit_lavaan@Options$likelihood
#> [1] "normal"
fit_eqs@Options$likelihood
#> [1] "wishart"

# Sample size: The same for fit_lavaan and fit_eqa
n <- nobs(fit_lavaan)

# lavaan Chi-square
# The values of the objective function
(fx_lavaan <- fit_lavaan@optim$fx)
#> [1] 0.1417035
# Self-computed chi-square
fx_lavaan * 2 * n
#> [1] 85.30552
# fitMeasures chi-square
print(fitMeasures(fit_lavaan, "chisq"), nd = 10)
#>    chisq
#> 85.30552

# EQS Chi-square
# The values of the objective function
(fx_eqs <- fit_eqs@optim$fx)
#> [1] 0.1417035
# Self-computed chi-square
fx_eqs * 2 * (n - 1)
#> [1] 85.02211
# fitMeasures chi-square
print(fitMeasures(fit_eqs, "chisq"), nd = 10)
#>    chisq
#> 85.02211
```

<sup>Created on 2023-06-14 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

When mimic = "lavaan", n, the sample size, is used in computing the model chi-square.

When mimic = "eqs", n - 1 is used instead.

Hope this helps.

P.S.: It would be great if there is a table summarizing all the effects of setting mimic to an option other than "lavaan", though I understand it may not be easy. Except for a few settings (e.g., likelihood), if a setting depends on mimic, the help page of lavOptions states that it depends but does not state how.

-- Shu Fai

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: chi-square comparison: Lavaan, Lisrel, and EQS
parts:
Chris,
This is not my area of expertise but your post brings two things to mind.  First, as I recall, LISREL offered perhaps a dozen different chi-square statistics.  So, if making comparisons it would be important to know which one you were looking at and which one should match another program's output.  Second, one well-known difference between LISREL and EQS is that LISREL defaulted to estimating unique variances and fixing the loadings to 1 whereas EQS defaulted to estimating the loadings and fixing the variances to 1.  As a result, any time LISREL converges on negative residual variance, one might expect a different chi-square value from EQS unless one has taken steps to over-ride these defaults in one or the other case.  Honestly, I am not sure how useful or interesting a benchmark LISREL provides at this point.  Have you considered comparing OpenMx?

Keith
